overview: The file consists of a two-page Department of State list of papers concerning petroleum policy in the Kwantung Leased Territory and Manchuria, followed by an apparently unrelated 1933 memorandum on a change in command of Japanese forces in Taiwan. The list indexes correspondence and consular reporting from late 1934 through September 1935 on the proposed oil monopoly, petroleum-trade regulations, the Manchuria Oil Company and Dairen refinery, gasoline storage at Port Arthur, crude-oil shipments, foreign-company activity, and a reported boycott by foreign oil firms. The final memorandum summarizes an August 1933 consular report and judges it to be of little interest.

subfiles.title: List of papers on petroleum in the Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.about: An internal index describes correspondence and consular reports concerning petroleum regulation, refining, imports, and the developing Japanese oil monopoly in the Kwantung Leased Territory and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: The list records papers dated from November 16, 1934, through September 6, 1935. It includes the Department's refusal to transmit an Export Petroleum Company letter to the Manchuria Oil Company, reports on gasoline tanks at Port Arthur and Japanese light-oil imports, and regulations implementing petroleum controls in the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway Zone. Later entries cover H. R. Greatwood's visit on behalf of Union Oil, the Dairen refinery, crude-oil deliveries, newspaper commentary, and a reported boycott of Japan and Manchukuo by foreign oil firms. Several entries note cross-filing under the Manchuria petroleum decimal-file classification.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the command of Japanese forces in Taiwan
subfiles.from: U.S. Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: The memorandum briefly evaluates a consular report on a change in command of Japanese forces in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum states that the consul at Taiwan reported to the Embassy on August 25 concerning a change in the command of Japanese forces. A statement by the new commanding general allegedly showed sympathy with the views of the ruling element in the Japanese Army. The memorandum concludes that the despatch was not of particular interest.

interest: The file index provides a compact chronological map of American diplomatic reporting on Japan's creation and enforcement of a controlled petroleum market in the Kwantung Leased Territory and Manchuria. It is especially useful for tracing the interaction of Japanese and Manchukuo policy with American oil companies, the Dairen refinery, shipping and storage infrastructure, and the State Department's reluctance to assist private approaches to the proposed monopoly. The unrelated Taiwan memorandum is also revealing as evidence of filing irregularities and of the Department's terse internal assessment of consular political reporting.
